answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: Akien's Q#93 answer about the ground loop applies to the bus. Also load-bearing: the kernel frees bus.lock when the holder dies, so --force can kill and retry the claim.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: the file and lines (server.py claim() ~832 and the held branch ~963-967; __main__.py argparse ~41-49); the exit semantics (0, silent); how --force finds a pid (decide and prove it); to run against a scratch CAIRN_BUS_HOME, never the live bus; and that bus_client is out. The ticket carries all of these except the pid mechanism, which is its first decision.

Horizon: the proof runs green twice on a scratch CAIRN_BUS_HOME and is red against the build's parent commit.
